performance.question: Is the observed cost the bottleneck in the user's workload?
rawEvidence: Per-trial samples, traces, allocations/GC, environment and workload identity
performance.technique: Experimental design: predeclare useful effect and tail limits; use paired AB/BA trials across sessions, treat trial medians rather than frames as replicates.
performance.falsifier: An unchanged control drifts, a tail regresses, or the actual journey does not improve.
performance.judge: Existing environment-qualified comparator plus correctness fixture; unavailable telemetry is unknown, never zero.

ui.question: Can the intended user complete the interaction at the constrained viewport?
rawEvidence: Rendered surface, semantic tree, keyboard/focus transitions, runtime errors, approved reference
ui.technique: Interaction design and accessibility: compare hierarchy against approved references; exercise narrow width, empty/error states and keyboard-only completion.
ui.falsifier: The control renders but cannot finish the task, loses focus, clips required content, or conflicts with a scoped approval.
ui.judge: Real browser interaction and computed geometry; human approval for unresolved taste. A screenshot alone proves neither.

animation.question: Does the action read correctly at gameplay distance and contact time?
rawEvidence: Effects-off full-cycle clips, source motion, signed joint angles, frame/pose strips and contact timestamps
animation.technique: Animation and perception: evaluate timing, silhouette and contact synchronization separately from VFX, then compare the combined gameplay result.
animation.falsifier: Finite transforms still contain knee flips, sliding contact, repeated frames or an unreadable silhouette.
animation.judge: Rig and cadence checks plus matched rendered references; quality remains scoped to actual human feedback.

architecture.question: Which real caller burden or recurring failure would the new boundary remove?
rawEvidence: Literal call sites, manifest/dependency edges, failing consumer, public imports, failure traces
architecture.technique: Systems engineering: model ownership and failure propagation; use compatibility matrices and real consumer probes before extraction.
architecture.falsifier: The proposed abstraction is already present, moves the same burden to callers, or has no demonstrated consumer.
architecture.judge: Existing public consumer tests and both named host paths; a static dependency graph is only discovery.

defect.question: What user outcome fails, and which causal hypothesis predicts that failure?
rawEvidence: Original input/seed, error stack, persisted state and failing interaction
defect.technique: Reliability engineering: reproduce the failure, isolate one cause, replay the original input and a held-out boundary/recovery case.
defect.falsifier: The reproduction still fails, or the fix only works in fresh state and fails after restart/retry.
defect.judge: Original reproduction plus independent runtime/state observation. Tests authored with the fix need an additional oracle.

release.question: Can the intended user complete first use and recovery with this exact candidate?
rawEvidence: Artifact hash/version/platform, extracted files, setup output, journey and recovery evidence
release.technique: Manufacturing QA and reproducibility: trace the delivered artifact, test outside the checkout and sample the critical failure/recovery boundary.
release.falsifier: The evidence belongs to a different build, checkout files hide a missing asset, or a planned/skipped gate appears passed.
release.judge: Existing ship-check JSON with explicit expected status plus installed/extracted journey; publication still needs authorization.

orchestration.question: Does scheduling reduce time to the verified outcome without losing ownership or recovery?
rawEvidence: Queue timestamps, lease/fence events, process lifetime, cancellation and partial-result receipts
orchestration.technique: Distributed systems and queueing: measure wait/service time, isolate independent work, inject lease loss and cancellation, verify idempotent recovery.
orchestration.falsifier: Throughput rises while verified latency, contention, duplicate work or orphaned processes worsen.
orchestration.judge: Durable lease and lifecycle tests plus observed end-to-end completion; additional agent opinions are not ground truth.
